A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OneTwoVLA. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables, equations and prompts, support reliable comparison. Retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original robot experiments, including long-horizon success rates, visual-grounding results, inference timings and appendix experiments on action multimodality.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and reports additional quantitative planning, recovery, interaction, timing and annotation-quality results.

M1.justification: V1 describes manually annotated robot reasoning. V2 introduces a two-stage Gemini annotation pipeline using sampled demonstration frames, interval identification and reasoning-content assembly, with recovery and dialogue extensions in Appendix D. This adds a substantial data-curation component. The controller architecture, losses and adaptive inference algorithm remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds testing on 20 novel human-robot interaction scenarios in Hotpot and Cocktail and describes interaction content in synthetic planning data. The three long-horizon tasks, four generalizable-planning tasks, grounding environments and robot platforms already appear in v1, including its appendices.

E2.justification: V2 Figure 6 adds π0 and robot-only OneTwoVLA comparisons on the existing generalizable-planning tasks; Figure 2 includes Dual-System in task-time comparisons. The original long-horizon and grounding comparator sets remain unchanged. Changing the dual-system baseline's cited inspiration from ViLa to Hi Robot does not establish a different Gemini-plus-π0 implementation.

E3.justification: V2 adds quantitative evaluation designs for generalizable planning, recovery conditional on errors, subtask-level interaction, novel interaction scenarios and annotation quality, including a 50-instance synthetic-data audit. Existing training budgets and grounding protocols are retained. Newly specifying the placement range and recovery-demonstration subsets does not establish that those settings changed.

E4.justification: V2 adds a with/without-VL comparison for generalizable planning, examines interaction generalization, evaluates automatic robot-annotation quality and audits synthetic-image/text errors. These substantially extend the analysis of co-training and data quality beyond v1's examples. Existing multimodality, reasoning-action consistency and failure-case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed replication, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The additional episode counts and audit frequencies in v2 provide sample sizes and results without introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The original long-horizon and grounding scores are retained. V2 newly reports generalizable-planning averages of 70% for OneTwoVLA-VL, 10% for OneTwoVLA and 6% for π0; quantitative recovery and interaction comparisons; 72.5% novel-interaction success; task timings; and annotation-quality findings, including 40 fully correct synthetic samples out of 50. These are added results, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: V2 Section 3.2 and Appendix D add formal specifications of ordered plans, reasoning intervals, history/next-step construction and dialogue-conditioned plan updates for automated annotation. The original policy formulation and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged, and no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution statements and conclusion retain the same central claims: unified adaptive reasoning and acting, synthetic vision-language co-training, and four demonstrated robot capabilities. The added methods and evidence do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: V2 reframes the annotation limitation around hand-selected reasoning-step heuristics and adds a potential action-inference bottleneck when scaling model size. It also interprets the new planning controls as showing limited generalization without VL co-training. Existing mechanism explanations and appendix failure cases remain.

D1.justification: V2 supplies substantial annotation instructions: 32-frame sampling, midpoint selection, content assembly, recovery/dialogue handling and complete prompt templates with output schemas and visibility/gripper constraints. It also discloses baseline invocation scheduling, placement randomization and recovery-data subsets. The existing training hardware, budgets and deployment details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds ECoT-Lite and discusses its reasoning-efficiency and interaction tradeoffs, changes the baseline's cited inspiration to Hi Robot, and removes several background references concerning recovery, interaction and reinforcement learning. The broad positioning against separated reasoning/action systems remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative sequence are retained, with localized method and experiment expansions. Co-training related work moves to Appendix B, conclusion and limitations are combined, and an LLM-usage statement is added. Author affiliations, acknowledgments, headings and citation style are also revised.

P2.justification: V1's long-horizon results table becomes a bar chart paired with new generalization results. V2 adds a timing chart, recovery and interaction tables, a quality-audit table and two annotation-prompt figures. It also adopts the ICLR layout and redistributes several appendix tables, environment illustrations and prompts across pages.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens capabilities supported mainly by examples in v1 through quantitative generalizable-planning, recovery and interaction comparisons. Annotation procedures and quality audits also address important documentation and evidence gaps while retaining the original benchmark results. Small recovery samples, absent uncertainty estimates and incomplete details behind the novel-interaction percentage limit the new evidence, but the overall improvement in empirical support and reproducibility is substantial.
